candidate.answerReason: The eleventh term is the middle term among the first 21 terms of an arithmetic sequence. Thus S_21=21a_11 and T_21=21b_11, giving the ratio 148:111=4:3.

methods.label: Use a sum centered on the eleventh term
methods.explanation:
In an arithmetic sequence, terms equally far from a middle term have that middle term as their average: the same number of common differences is added on one side and subtracted on the other. This suggests using the first \(21\) terms, whose middle term is the eleventh.

Let \(a_{11}\) and \(b_{11}\) be the eleventh terms of the two sequences. In the first sequence, each of the ten pairs surrounding \(a_{11}\) sums to \(2a_{11}\). Including the middle term gives
\[
S_{21}=21a_{11}.
\]
The same reasoning gives \(T_{21}=21b_{11}\). The stated ratio is defined at \(n=21\), so \(T_{21}\ne0\), and consequently \(b_{11}\ne0\). Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{a_{11}}{b_{11}}
&=\frac{S_{21}}{T_{21}}\\
&=\frac{7\cdot21+1}{4\cdot21+27}\\
&=\frac{148}{111}=\frac43.
\end{aligned}
\]
The required ratio is \(\boxed{4:3}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
